A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MapDR research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and image-based figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MapDR benchmark results, component ablations, per-lane evaluations, five-seed analyses and evaluations of MLLMs on 180 cases.

after.justification: v2 retains original modular-model experiments and adds empirical evaluations of a heuristic, trained Qwen-VL prompt approaches and RuleVLM.

M1.justification: Section 6 adds RuleVLM, an end-to-end model combining Qwen-VL with MEE vector encoding, a trainable adapter and LoRA fine-tuning to generate serialized driving rules and lane associations. The original modular VLE-MEE procedure is retained; its revised classification-head description matches details already present in v1's appendix.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MapDR coverage of Chinese traffic signs and lane-rule association across Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou, including the same lane categories and 180-case zero-shot subset. The end-to-end models address the existing overall task. The newly stated approximately 800 km does not establish expanded data collection.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds an OCR/nearest-lane heuristic and trained Qwen-VL TextPrompt and VisualPrompt comparisons. v1's unnamed baseline already adapts ALBEF and BERT; its appearance as ALBEF-BERT in v2 is a rename, not an additional comparator. The four zero-shot MLLMs remain in appendix Table 5.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 replaces AP with F1 for benchmark ranking. Section 6 introduces QA-formatted supervised fine-tuning experiments with 20 training epochs and specified LoRA settings. Appendix J also changes the stated zero-shot accuracy criterion from v1's rule/edge-overlap ratios to whole-sign correctness, without establishing whether those evaluations were rerun. The modular 9:1 split and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6 adds a substantive investigation of centerline representation: textual coordinates, visual overlays and learned MEE tokens, comparing their effects on rule extraction and overall association performance. Existing modular attention/embedding ablations, per-lane analyses and qualitative zero-shot examples are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix J.3 and v2 Appendix I.4 report the same five seeds, precision-recall curves and standard deviations for the modular method. No new uncertainty reporting accompanies the end-to-end results. The retained appendix still reports AP uncertainty despite the main benchmark switching to F1.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds heuristic and end-to-end results, including F1 scores of 0.083, 0.392 and 0.642 for TextPrompt, VisualPrompt and RuleVLM. VLE-MEE's precision/recall values remain unchanged; AP 44.60% is replaced by F1 0.653, which is not a comparable performance increase. Previously nonconvergent baseline C.R. entries become 4.14% precision and 17.25% recall. Appendix Table 5 removes the Ours results of 65.15% and 78.84%.

T1.justification: The zero-shot scoring definition changes from fractions of correct rules and edges in v1 Appendix K to whole-sign correctness in v2 Appendix J. This revises the mathematical scoring unit. The bipartite-graph framework and worked precision/recall derivations remain substantively unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v1 presents the dataset/task and modular VLE-MEE baseline, leaving further MLLM modeling to future work. v2 makes both modular and RuleVLM end-to-end solutions central contributions. Its abstract, introduction and conclusion also explicitly frame MapDR as supporting the traffic-regulation layer of online HD maps.

C2.justification: v2 adds mechanism interpretations linking coordinate-prompt length, visual spatial reasoning and learned vector features to end-to-end performance. It replaces the baseline nonconvergence explanation with inadequate adaptation to vector information. It also removes v1's explicit limitation excluding dynamic elements such as traffic lights, while retaining the existing Chinese-OCR and visual-prompt caveats.

D1.justification: v2 adds heuristic implementation details, Qwen-VL initialization, LoRA settings, trainable/frozen components, A6000 hardware and JSON schemas. It removes v1 Appendix E's specific dataset/evaluation-code request instructions and the PyTorch-version and optimizer/scheduler disclosures. The new label schema also excludes Bus and time-range strings used in documented examples; this is a documentation inconsistency, not evidence that dataset coverage changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds HD-map surveys, Navigation Data Standard and TopoMLP references supporting its three-layer framing, together with ViT, LoRA and additional LLM-driving citations. The SGDR and AdamW references disappear. The central positioning against CTSU, VTKGG and OpenLane-V2 remains, so the related-work argument is refined rather than replaced.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around HD-map layers, and Section 3 introduces the overall task before its subtasks. The narrative is reorganized into modular and end-to-end approaches, with a rewritten conclusion, revised appendix organization and a contents list. These changes substantially exceed local copyediting.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws Figure 1 to display HD-map layers, revises Figure 4 and adds the end-to-end architecture Figure 8. Table 2 gains method-type groups and an F1 column, while composition tables become schema listings. Existing appendix visual examples are enlarged and separately numbered rather than newly added cases.

improvement.justification: v1's main overall comparison offered only a nonconvergent alternative. v2 supplies evaluated heuristic and trained prompt alternatives and investigates how vector encoding affects end-to-end integration (Table 2 and Section 6), substantially strengthening comparative validation and the benchmark's usefulness. These gains outweigh documentation regressions: removed access instructions, inconsistencies in the new label schema, and AP uncertainty retained after switching to F1. The improvement rests on stronger comparative evidence, not higher reported scores or revision size.
